note: AI-drafted proposals for links between the Social-Core and Computational-Core spaces and German and US curriculum policy records. Every row is loaded as a proposed link (relation type starts with proposed_) for a person to confirm, edit or remove. Source: two drafting passes grounded in the record titles and summaries; see the design note.

links.rationale: The KMK names cross-subject teaching as one of three pillars of democracy education, under a goal of tolerant and democratic living together. It gives the national frame in which a strand on groups, rules and institutions would sit in Germany.
links.recordTitle: KMK/Bildungsministerkonferenz names Faecherubergreifendes Unterrichtsprinzip as one of three pillars of Demokratiebildung, nationally, for 2025

links.rationale: Describes Sozialkunde and G/R/W outside the Gymnasium in Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt and Thüringen as covering civics, law, economics and international relations. It points to where rules and institutions are taught in these states.
links.recordTitle: Sozialkunde/G-R-W's absence of human-origins content is confirmed across all three states' non-Gymnasium tracks, closing the last subject-coverage gap

links.rationale: Lower Saxony put a Kerncurriculum for Werte und Normen in grades 1 to 4 out for consultation in February 2026. The subject name points to values and rules in early schooling. Only the title is available, so the fit is untested.
links.objectTitle: Groups We Belong To and Their Rules
links.recordTitle: Kerncurricula in Anhörung: Mathematik Grundschule, Christliche Religion 5-10, Werte und Normen 1-4

links.rationale: The same Lower Saxony consultation covers Werte und Normen for grades 1 to 4, which overlaps this grades 3 to 5 band. The title gives no detail on roles or on why rules differ, so the fit is a candidate for checking.
links.recordTitle: Kerncurricula in Anhörung: Mathematik Grundschule, Christliche Religion 5-10, Werte und Normen 1-4

links.rationale: Eight Dover biology teachers refused to read a school-board disclaimer, citing their profession's ethics code, and administrators read it instead. A case where a professional norm and an authority's rule pull apart, usable for sorting peer-held norms from enforced rules.
links.recordTitle: All 8 Dover biology teachers refuse to read the disclaimer; it is read by administrators instead

links.rationale: Notes that the Butler Act was enforced exactly once in 42 years and the 2012 Teacher Protection Act apparently never. It treats both as mandates teachers must still account for, which suits the question of what a rarely enforced rule still does.
links.recordTitle: A law nobody has prosecuted under, or ever invoked, is still a real curriculum mandate worth documenting precisely

links.rationale: Saxony's Gymnasium G/R/W plan builds the subject on analytic categories such as Macht and Institutionen, together with law and negotiated order. This matches the item's focus on formal institutions and power.
links.recordTitle: G/R/W's own foundational categories (Macht, Institutionen, Recht...) <-> evolved reliance on institutions for large-scale non-kin cooperation

links.rationale: Traces how Supreme Court rulings in 1968 and 1987 ended certain teaching bans and mandates, after which new laws appeared in forms built to avoid the defect the Court named. It shows an institution reshaping the options people face.
links.recordTitle: A landmark ruling changes what the next legislative attempt looks like; it rarely ends the underlying attempt

links.rationale: Sets Florida's negotiated 2008 wording on evolution beside Pennsylvania's Dover case, which a federal court decided on the constitutional question. A board vote and a court settle the same kind of dispute in different ways, which suits the item's comparison of institutions.
links.recordTitle: A court ruling can settle a curriculum dispute more durably than a subsequent vote, where a constitutional question is actually at stake

links.rationale: Records eight Dover teachers' collective refusal to read a district disclaimer, citing their profession's ethics code, as a check on curriculum governance. It gives a case for sorting a formal board policy from an informal professional norm.
links.recordTitle: Teachers refusing to implement a mandate they judge unscientific is itself a documentable form of curriculum governance

links.rationale: An OpenEvo brief proposes that Cooperation Games and Governing the Commons content can supply evidence for New York's Global Citizen attribute. It points to where cooperation teaching could sit in a US state framework.
links.recordTitle: Map OpenEvo's content anchors directly onto the Portrait's attributes as ready-to-use content, not a competing framework

links.rationale: Saxony's grade 10 economics goals teach an idealized rational-actor model, which the record sets against cross-cultural ultimatum-game findings on fairness. It is a later-grade treatment of this item's question of why people give or keep.
links.objectTitle: Why People Cooperate or Hold Back
links.recordTitle: Wirtschaft und Wirtschaftsordnung (Kl. 10) <-> evolved fairness/reciprocity psychology vs. the idealtypische homo-oeconomicus model

links.rationale: Saxony's Gymnasium G/R/W plan puts Macht and Konflikt among its central analytic categories, alongside institutions and negotiated rules. These are the ideas this item uses to compare governance designs and judge the part power plays.
links.objectTitle: Governing Shared Resources: Power and Conflict
links.recordTitle: G/R/W's own foundational categories (Macht, Institutionen, Recht...) <-> evolved reliance on institutions for large-scale non-kin cooperation

links.rationale: Argues that global citizenship teaching needs an account of why cooperation at scale is hard, built on evolved cooperation mechanisms and the psychology of institutions. This item builds its account from power, conflict and institutions, so the two can be compared.
links.objectTitle: Governing Shared Resources: Power and Conflict
links.recordTitle: Global Citizen attribute <-> evolved cooperation and the psychology of institutions

links.rationale: An OpenEvo brief maps the Governing the Commons content anchor onto New York's Global Citizen attribute. It shows one US state framework in which content on governing shared resources could be placed.
links.objectTitle: Governing Shared Resources: Power and Conflict
links.recordTitle: Map OpenEvo's content anchors directly onto the Portrait's attributes as ready-to-use content, not a competing framework

links.rationale: Saxony's grade 11 plan asks students to learn theories of international relations and to analyze international conflicts. It extends this item's questions about power and conflict to the international scale.
links.objectTitle: Governing Shared Resources: Power and Conflict
links.recordTitle: Internationale Politik (Jgst. 11) <-> evolved intergroup cooperation/conflict and the security dilemma

links.rationale: The title says North Rhine-Westphalia revised its Kernlehrplan for Gesellschaftslehre in the Hauptschule. That plan is a candidate source on how a German state teaches about societies. No text is available, so the fit is untested.
links.objectTitle: Social Change and Diversity of Societies
links.recordTitle: Kernlehrplan im Lernbereich Gesellschaftslehre (Hauptschule) novellierten

links.rationale: The title says Saarland published new Gemeinschaftsschule curricula for 2025/26, among them one for Gesellschaftswissenschaften. It is a candidate source for how a German state frames social studies. No text is available, so the fit is untested.
links.objectTitle: Social Change and Diversity of Societies
links.recordTitle: New Gemeinschaftsschule curricula published for 2025/26: Gesellschaftswissenschaften, Naturwissenschaften, integrated Informatik

links.rationale: Sachsen-Anhalt's Sekundarschule Geographie covers population development in regions of Asia at grades 7/8. A regional comparison of this kind could supply evidence when students explain why societies differ.
links.recordTitle: Sachsen-Anhalt Sekundarschule Geographie: Bevölkerungsentwicklung in two touches, both at or before Gymnasium's placement

links.rationale: Compares Florida, Pennsylvania and Tennessee, which currently take three different postures on evolution education, each with its own history of standards, litigation or statute. It is a cross-state comparison of the kind this item asks students to make.
links.recordTitle: Florida, Pennsylvania, and Tennessee have three genuinely different current postures on evolution-education policy

links.rationale: Follows one question in Tennessee over a century, from a 1925 prohibition to a 1973 equal-emphasis mandate and a later law in secular language. A worked case of courts and legislators shaping each other over generations.
links.recordTitle: When a recurring legislative fight loses in court, the next round tends to arrive in secularized language, not a changed goal

links.rationale: Describes how one question about teaching human origins recurred across US states and decades, from Tennessee's 1925 law to the Arkansas and Mississippi bans and later cases. It gives a long-run case for evaluating explanations of change.
links.recordTitle: The American evolution-education culture war, 1925-present

links.rationale: Reports that a model Academic Freedom Act template from the Discovery Institute was enacted in Louisiana in 2008 and Tennessee in 2012, and used for Florida bills. A documented case of a policy spreading between states.
links.recordTitle: The 2008 "Academic Freedom Act" (SB 2692/HB 1483) legislative fight

itemsWithoutLinks.why: The corpus has no early-grade record on local history or community change, such as Sachunterricht or K-2 social studies.

social.corpusGaps: The corpus has no records on early-grade social learning in either country, such as Sachunterricht in Germany or K-2 social studies in the US, so the K-2 items and the Shared-Resource Problems item have nothing to attach to. It also lacks any record on commons governance, public goods or collective-action cases taught in schools. Records from social-studies, civics and Gesellschaftslehre curricula are scarce: the usable German ones are a few Saxon G/R/W and Sozialkunde findings plus title-only timeline entries, and the only US civics-adjacent material is a set of New York graduate-profile briefs. Cross-curricular principle records, such as the Leitperspektiven in Baden-Württemberg and Hamburg, the Medienkompetenz supplement in Schleswig-Holstein and the Demokratiebildung entry, are mostly timeline events with empty text, so their fit cannot be judged. Nearly all US records concern evolution and climate education, and the few linked here are governance cases (courts, school boards, legislatures) that a curator should treat as bridge cases. Full-text records of German state Lehrpläne for Gesellschaftslehre, Politik, Sozialkunde and Geschichte, and of US state social-studies and civics standards, would let most of these items be linked on content.

links.rationale: Baden-Württemberg makes Informatik und Medienbildung a compulsory subject from grade 5, with its own Bildungsplan planned for 2027/28. This strand starts in K-2, so the record shows a later entry point for the same question of when computing begins. Title only.
links.recordTitle: New Pflichtfach 'Informatik und Medienbildung' taught from grade 5; own Bildungsplan 2027/28

links.rationale: Bremen makes Informatik a compulsory subject at all its secondary schools from August 2026. It shows one state giving computing its own required place in the timetable, which is a point of comparison for this K-12 strand. Only the title is available.
links.recordTitle: Informatik becomes a compulsory subject at all Bremen secondary schools

links.rationale: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern gives Informatik und Medienbildung a standalone place in its 2025/26 timetable changes. It is a second example of a state placing computing in its own subject, useful for comparison with this strand. The record has a title only.
links.recordTitle: Stundentafel and subject changes for 2025/26: Informatik und Medienbildung standalone, Geschichte from grade 5, Chemie from grade 7

links.rationale: Thüringen introduced Medienbildung und Informatik (MBI) in August 2024. The title gives no grade or content, so the link to this strand rests on the subject name alone.
links.recordTitle: Medienbildung und Informatik (MBI) introduced

links.rationale: Sachsen makes Informatik compulsory in grades 7-10, while Sachsen-Anhalt offers it as an elective from grade 9 and Thüringen from grade 9/10. This is a different treatment from a strand that runs from K through grade 12.
links.recordTitle: All three states independently center Informatik on the same 'Modellieren' competency, despite differing on compulsory status and grade

links.rationale: The three states center Informatik on 'Modellieren', yet the subject begins in grade 7 at the earliest. This substrand has students build models of everyday systems in grades 3-5. The German term may cover more than simulation, which needs checking.
links.objectTitle: Models and Simulations of Everyday Systems
links.recordTitle: All three states independently center Informatik on the same 'Modellieren' competency, despite differing on compulsory status and grade

links.rationale: Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt and Thüringen each build Informatik around informatische Modellierung, with Sachsen teaching it in grades 7-10. That is the closest German counterpart to the model-building focus of this grades 6-8 substrand, although the German term may cover more than simulation.
links.recordTitle: All three states independently center Informatik on the same 'Modellieren' competency, despite differing on compulsory status and grade

links.rationale: Sachsen's 2022 Oberschule Informatik and Sachsen-Anhalt's new Sekundarschule Informatik also center on Modellieren, and the latter lists 'Modellieren und Implementieren' among five core competency areas. This adds a second school type to the evidence for this substrand's focus.
links.recordTitle: The cross-state 'Modellieren' Informatik convergence extends to two more non-Gymnasium tracks

links.rationale: Sachsen-Anhalt's Sekundarschule Informatik pairs 'Modellieren' with 'Implementieren' as one of five core competency areas. That sits next to this substrand's work on splitting problems into functions. The match is loose, so check how the source describes 'Implementieren'.
links.recordTitle: The cross-state 'Modellieren' Informatik convergence extends to two more non-Gymnasium tracks

links.rationale: KMK names systemic thinking and handling complexity among five criteria for sustainability-oriented teaching (June 2024). That gives a national policy hook for the feedback models in this substrand, although the record concerns sustainability education in general.
links.recordTitle: KMK names fachuebergreifendes/faecherverbindendes Lernen as a core BNE criterion

links.rationale: The national ministers' conference adopted a recommendation for action on AI in school education in October 2024. It gives the policy background for this machine learning substrand. The record has a title only, so what it asks of schools needs checking.
links.objectTitle: Machine Learning, Search and Distributed Systems Compared
links.recordTitle: Bildungsministerkonferenz adopts Handlungsempfehlung on AI in school education

links.rationale: This synthetic redesign proposal for Thüringen frames the hormone system as an information-processing system, a Biologie and Informatik bridge. It touches the idea of information, though the sense may differ from bits and compression. Title only.
links.objectTitle: Information, Compression and the Limits of Representation
links.recordTitle: A Proposed Biologie/Informatik Bridge: Modeling the Hormone System as an Information-Processing System

computational.corpusGaps: The corpus has no US record on computing, computer science, data science or digital literacy, because the US records cover evolution-education disputes and graduation frameworks. A curator would need to add state computer-science and technology standards for the states already tracked (New York, Florida, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, California). On the German side, Informatik appears mostly as dated timeline events with no text (Bremen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Baden-Württemberg, Thüringen), so each needs a written summary of grade placement, compulsory status and competency areas. The only content-level Informatik records are the Modellieren findings for Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt and Thüringen secondary schools. Nothing covers primary-school computing, data and representation, algorithm correctness and efficiency, or the national digital-education strategy, and the media-education and AI items exist as titles only.
